clue.text: Mad about old crooner causing injury

indicators.note: about signals that the word for mad is turned round and read the other way

parts.note: bats is slang for mad or crazy
Bing Crosby was a famous crooner of the mid-twentieth century

explanation.surface: A deranged fan of a vintage singer lashes out and hurts someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the reversal signal; 'causing injury' works as the definition since a stabbing pain hurts.
explanation.definitionFit: A stabbing pain or attack is one that wounds, so the adjective describes something that hurts.

clue.text: Chew gum, initially, before turning pale

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the word gum is used
turning tells us the word for pale is read backwards here

parts.note: wan means pale or sickly-looking

explanation.surface: Someone works at a piece of gum before going pale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letter of 'gum'; 'turning' is the reversal signal, and 'before' just places the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to bite at something repeatedly with the teeth; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Liven up article about funeral vigil

indicators.note: about here means the article goes around the vigil, holding it inside

parts.note: an is the indefinite article in grammar
a wake is a watch kept over a body before burial

explanation.surface: Instructions for enlivening a newspaper piece about a mourning gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' means the article wraps around the vigil, not that the article is on the subject of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse something or bring it to life is to stir it from sleep or dullness; synonyms.

clue.text: A general in a sheltered spot

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: A military commander takes cover somewhere protected.
explanation.walkthrough: A is given as written, followed by LEE, the Civil War general.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautically, on the side away from the wind is the protected side, sheltered from gusts.

clue.text: ill: quart drunk

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'ill: quart drunk (4,6)': the opening words are missing; ILLQUART is only eight of the ten letters, so the M and O pieces and the definition are lost.

clue.text: Join one new sailor

parts.note: a seam is the line where two pieces are joined, so it can stand for join
a is used to mean one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: An order to sign up a fresh recruit to the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: SEAM (join), A (one) and N (new) run side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A mariner or naval rating who works on ships at sea is a synonym for this.

clue.text: One that's cross flying north today?

definitions.text: One that's cross flying north today?

parts.words: One that's cross flying north today?
parts.note: the saltire, the diagonal cross of Scotland's patron saint, flies north of the border on his feast day, 30 November, when the puzzle ran

explanation.surface: An irritable person heading north on a particular day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' suggests anger, but it is the saltire flag; 'north' means Scotland, whose patron saint's day is 30 November.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland's patron saint has a diagonal cross on its flag, flown on his feast day.

clue.text: Sun dried off bathers, ultimately producing healthy complexion

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or spoilt, so the letters of sun dried are jumbled
ultimately points to only the final letter of the word bathers

explanation.surface: Swimmers who have dried off in the sunshine end up with rosy cheeks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SUNDRIED to RUDDINE; 'ultimately' adds the last letter of 'bathers', S.
explanation.definitionFit: A reddish, glowing colouring of the face is taken as a sign of good health.

clue.text: Like some lights, shot through with a metallic element?

definitions.text: shot through with a metallic element?

explanation.surface: A description of lamps, or of something riddled with heavy metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lights' are windows: stained glass panes are held in strips of lead. 'Shot through' also hints at lead shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Windows framed in metal strips are described this way, and so is anything containing the heavy metal Pb.

clue.text: Bent bachelor was in debt

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in a degree
someone who owed money was in debt

explanation.surface: A stooped single man who owed money.
explanation.walkthrough: B (bachelor) then OWED (was in debt).
explanation.definitionFit: Curved or stooped forward, as a head or back bent over; synonyms.

clue.text: is something conductor should do

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'is something conductor should do (4,4)': the opening words, holding the wordplay or the first definition, are missing.

clue.text: Underworld team running into a loss of direction

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and his realm
Leyton Orient is a London football team, often just called Orient

indicators.note: running suggests the letters of into a are in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: A team from the underworld charges into a state of confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: Leyton Orient is a London football club. 'running' rearranges INTO A to ATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing your bearings, being unable to tell which way is which, is a state of confusion.

clue.text: In public each group of pupils comes to excel

parts.note: something out is in the open, known publicly
per means for each, as in per head
a form is a school class in British schools

explanation.surface: Every class in a school does well when it performs in public.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a FORM is a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass others or do better than them is to be outstanding; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Person completing envelope one day on kitchen cupboard

parts.note: a means one, a single thing
a dresser is a kitchen sideboard with shelves for crockery

explanation.surface: Someone writing an envelope one day while leaning on a kitchen unit.
explanation.walkthrough: A (one) and D (day) sit 'on' DRESSER, a British kitchen cabinet with open shelves above.
explanation.definitionFit: The one who writes the name and destination on a letter's cover is its writer of directions.

clue.text: Processed fish leading to upset?

explanation.surface: Preparing fish leads to someone being distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: A fish is cleaned by removing its insides; British slang also uses the word for bitterly disappointed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish prepared by removing the entrails are described thus, and in slang it means devastated.

clue.text: Make minor changes in our time only

parts.note: AD, Anno Domini, labels the years of the current era
just means only, as in just one

explanation.surface: Tweaking things only within the present era.
explanation.walkthrough: AD (our era) then JUST (only).
explanation.definitionFit: To tweak or alter something slightly so it fits better; synonyms.

clue.text: Do a front decoratively going backwards and forwards

indicators.note: decoratively suggests the letters of do a front are arranged in a new, ornamental pattern

explanation.surface: Advice to dress up a shopfront while moving back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decoratively' rearranges DOAFRONT.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving one way and then the other repeatedly; the idiom means oscillating.

clue.text: Practice for which you've to get into the habit?

definitions.text: Practice for which you've to get into the habit?

parts.words: Practice for which you've to get into the habit?
parts.note: habit is a costume, so getting into it means wearing stage clothes for a final run-through

explanation.surface: Some routine you must make a regular part of your life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get into the habit' seems to mean form a routine, but a habit is a garment: actors wear costume at the last rehearsal.
explanation.definitionFit: The final run-through of a play performed in full costume before opening night.

clue.text: TV characters changing places to pour wine?

indicators.note: changing places means the two names swap round, the second coming first

parts.note: Ant and Dec are a British TV presenting duo

explanation.surface: Television figures swap seats before serving the wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a well-known British TV presenting pair; 'changing places' swaps them to DEC ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: To transfer wine from bottle into a carafe, leaving sediment behind, is this verb.

clue.text: Swirled around as Edward faded

parts.note: Ed is a short form of the name Edward
died can mean faded away, as a sound or light dies

explanation.surface: Edward grew weak and his head spun.
explanation.walkthrough: ED (Edward) then DIED (faded).
explanation.definitionFit: Water that circled in small whirlpools did this; synonyms for moving in a spiral.

clue.text: Structure of old penal system

explanation.surface: A description of the framework behind historic punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Builders' framework of poles, and the platform on which criminals were once hanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Builders' temporary framework, and the platform once used for public executions.

clue.text: Stone animal on outskirts of city

indicators.note: on outskirts of means the animal sits around the city, enclosing it

parts.note: an ox is a bovine animal
NY is the abbreviation for New York city

explanation.surface: A statue of a creature on the edge of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on outskirts of' means the animal surrounds the city, rather than standing beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A banded variety of chalcedony used as a gemstone; an example of a stone.

clue.text: Rushes round to get valuable instrument

indicators.note: round means the word for rushes is turned about and read backwards

parts.note: darts means rushes or dashes

explanation.surface: Someone dashes about to obtain a precious violin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' reverses DARTS (rushes); a STRAD is a Stradivarius violin.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stradivarius is a hugely prized violin, so this short form names a costly fiddle.

clue.text: Managed to get Dutch and South African currency

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: Someone succeeded in getting both Dutch and South African money.
explanation.walkthrough: RAN (managed) then D (Dutch); 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The monetary unit used in South Africa, named after the Witwatersrand ridge.

clue.text: Things to be dealt with by leaderless party, possibly

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Things to be dealt with by leaderless party, possibly (2-4)': (P)ARTY rearranged gives TRAY, but no word supplies IN; 'by' may be an OCR misread, unconfirmed.
annotationWithheld.clue: Things to be dealt with by leaderless party, possibly

clue.text: Wandering monarch organised an attempt to follow

indicators.note: to follow means the attempt comes after the earlier pieces

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the monarch
ran means organised, as in ran an event
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A roaming king set up a try that came next.
explanation.walkthrough: ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the crossword's usual monarch; 'to follow' puts the attempt last.
explanation.definitionFit: Roving in search of adventure, like a knight-errant, is the sense of this noun.
